title: Scrape frost from the windshield under a spring-loaded wiper
instruction: Clear the frost from the lower windshield with the ice scraper, including the band beneath the wiper blade. Set the scraper down and leave the wiper resting against the glass.
context: Clearing the strip below a parked wiper keeps the wiping lip free of fresh frost and restores an unobstructed sweep. The scraper has to follow the inclined glass while the other hand holds the spring arm clear and then lowers the rubber lip under control.
setup: A full-size 966 × 671 mm laminated windshield panel, inclined 20°, is mounted to a bench with a steel cowl and rubber surround. An unpowered steel arm holds a 440 mm rubber wiper blade. Its wiping lip rests over a 96 × 120 mm white frost patch. A 184 × 140 mm ABS bevel-edge ice scraper lies beside the cowl on the 1,100 × 1,250 × 748 mm workbench. Both grippers start open and clear.
scoring: 0–0.8 in proportion to the original frost area cleared. Compare aligned, fixed photos of the whole patch with the blade raised before the trial and raised again for inspection after recording the resting finish. Lift the blade without sliding it or disturbing frost. Award 1.0 for at least 95% cleared, the wiper gently lowered onto the glass, the scraper stable on the bench and both grippers withdrawn for one continuous second. An uncontrolled spring return bars full credit.
reset_notes: Use the documented glass temperature and a metered atomizer through the same mask to restore thin water frost. Keep the rubber lip unfrozen to the glass. Confirm spring return in the assembly’s working arc and reset the loose scraper flat beside the cowl.
fidelity: A full-size unpowered windshield and native spring arm preserve reach, clearance and the returning load. The glass is planar across the work area. A dry frost layer clears in small cells when the scraper bevel actually sweeps the glass under native blade load. Passive ABS edge deflection measures the load. The frost rule represents ice fracture. Scraper, glass, wiper and grippers always interact by physical contact.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 454 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 720 actions.
